title: An agent buys one API call: discovery, x402 exact payment, ERC-8004 feedback
summary: A client agent finds a paid weather endpoint through the x402 Bazaar or an ERC-8004 registration, pays for one call with x402 V2 exact (EIP-3009 on an EVM chain, gas paid by the facilitator), then publishes an off-chain feedback file carrying proofOfPayment and calls giveFeedback with its URI and hash.

steps.label: GET /discovery/resources (Bazaar)
steps.detail: Path A. The client asks a facilitator's Bazaar for paid resources, filtered by type, scheme and network. Each listing repeats the accepts entries the server will demand, so the client can see the price before it calls.
steps.controlPoint: Before authorization: allowlist sellers and networks; treat a listing as a claim by the seller, not a check of the seller.
steps.observable: Public: the Bazaar listing (resource URL, accepts entries, lastUpdated) can be read by anyone; the CDP instance needs no API key.

failures.condition: The listing is stale and the server now asks for more
failures.outcome: The live 402 response wins; the client must compare it with its budget again.

steps.label: Read tokenURI and getAgentWallet (ERC-8004)
steps.detail: Path B. The client knows the seller's agentId and reads the agentURI and the verified payment address agentWallet from the Identity Registry. A careful client also reads getSummary from the Reputation Registry, filtered to reviewers it trusts.
steps.controlPoint: Before authorization: require a minimum reputation from a curated reviewer list; refuse agents whose NFT changed owner since the wallet was bound.
steps.observable: Public: Registered, URIUpdated, MetadataSet and Transfer events; reads are free and leave no trace on chain.

failures.outcome: agentWallet was cleared on transfer; getAgentWallet returns no wallet until the new owner binds one again.

steps.label: Fetch the registration file
steps.detail: The agentURI resolves to the registration file. The client reads the services list and x402Support. An HTTPS file can change without any on-chain event, so a client that relies on it should prefer content-addressed or data: URIs, and can check the /.well-known domain proof.

payload.content:
// Illustrative example, spec version Draft 2026-01-25.
{
  "type": "https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8004#registration-v1",
  "name": "weather-agent",
  "description": "Current weather per city, paid per call",
  "image": "https://api.weather.example/logo.png",
  "services": [ { "name": "web", "endpoint": "https://api.weather.example/" } ],
  "x402Support": true,
  "active": true,
  "registrations": [ { "agentId": 123456789, "agentRegistry": "eip155:8453:0x8004A169FB4a3325136EB29fA0ceB6D2e539a432" } ],
  "supportedTrust": [ "reputation" ]
}

specRef.section: Agent URI and Agent Registration File

steps.controlPoint: At the edge: match the serving domain against the registration file and https://{endpoint-domain}/.well-known/agent-registration.json.
steps.observable: Public: the registration file at the agentURI and the optional /.well-known domain proof.

failures.condition: The file is gone or does not list the endpoint
failures.outcome: Nothing on chain flags it; the client should not pay that endpoint.

steps.label: GET /weather (no payment header)
steps.detail: The client calls the endpoint like any HTTP request. It sends no PAYMENT-SIGNATURE header yet.

payload.content:
# Illustrative example, spec version x402 v2.0.
GET /weather?city=Lisbon HTTP/1.1
Host: api.weather.example

steps.label: 402 Payment Required with PAYMENT-REQUIRED
steps.detail: The server answers 402. The PAYMENT-REQUIRED header holds base64 JSON with x402Version, resource and an accepts list; here one exact entry for 10000 atomic units (0.01 of a 6-decimal stablecoin) on a CAIP-2 network.
steps.controlPoint: Before authorization: client policy and SDK spendControls decide whether to pay at all (default: default assets only, at most $1 per payment in the TypeScript SDK).
steps.observable: Private: the 402 and its header travel only between client and server.

steps.label: Check payTo against agentWallet, sign EIP-3009
steps.detail: The client picks the exact entry, checks that payTo equals the agentWallet it read in step 2 (path B), and signs EIP-712 typed data for TransferWithAuthorization over from, to, value, validAfter, validBefore and a random 32-byte nonce. No transaction is sent and no gas is spent by the client.
steps.controlPoint: At signing: a short validBefore window, a wallet signing policy, and a payee check against ERC-8004 agentWallet.

failures.condition: payTo differs from the agent's agentWallet
failures.outcome: Neither protocol forces this check; a client that skips it can pay an address the agent never verified.

failures.condition: The amount is above the spend cap
failures.outcome: The SDK rejects the entry and no payment is created.

steps.label: Retry with PAYMENT-SIGNATURE
steps.detail: The client repeats the request with a base64 PaymentPayload in the PAYMENT-SIGNATURE header: x402Version, resource, accepted (the chosen entry), payload (signature and authorization) and extensions.

payload.content:
# Illustrative example, spec version x402 v2.0.
GET /weather?city=Lisbon HTTP/1.1
Host: api.weather.example
PAYMENT-SIGNATURE: eyJ4NDAyVmVyc2lvbiI6MiwicmVzb3VyY2UiOn...

steps.controlPoint: At the edge: payment middleware or a CDN gateway can inspect the request before it reaches the handler.

steps.label: POST /verify, run the handler
steps.detail: The server sends x402Version, paymentPayload and its own paymentRequirements to /verify. The facilitator recovers the signer, checks recipient, amount, time window, balance and nonce, and writes nothing. On isValid true the server runs the handler; funds have not moved yet.

failures.condition: isValid is false (for example insufficient_funds or invalid_exact_evm_payload_signature)
failures.outcome: The server answers 402 again and the handler does not run.
The server does not settle, so the client is not charged.

steps.label: POST /settle
steps.detail: The server sends the same body to /settle. The facilitator commits payment state by broadcasting the signed authorization.
steps.controlPoint: At settlement: facilitator sanctions and KYT screening (the CDP facilitator runs OFAC and Know Your Transaction checks), onBeforeSettle hooks, deduplication across settle workers.

failures.condition: The settle call times out or returns settlement_pending
failures.outcome: The outcome is indeterminate; the server must reconcile the broadcast hash before it retries.

steps.label: transferWithAuthorization (facilitator pays gas)
steps.detail: On the EVM exact path the facilitator submits the authorization to the token contract and pays the gas. The contract checks signature, window and nonce and moves exactly value to payTo. The facilitator cannot change the amount or the recipient.
steps.observable: Public: an ordinary token Transfer plus AuthorizationUsed event; nothing on chain marks it as an x402 payment.

failures.condition: The nonce was used or the balance dropped
failures.outcome: The transaction reverts and the facilitator returns success false.

steps.label: 200 OK with PAYMENT-RESPONSE
steps.detail: The server returns the weather data and a PAYMENT-RESPONSE header holding the base64 SettleResponse: success, payer, transaction (the hash), network and amount. The transaction hash becomes the txHash of proofOfPayment.

payload.content:
# Illustrative example, spec version x402 v2.0.
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json
PAYMENT-RESPONSE: eyJzdWNjZXNzIjp0cnVlLC...

# decoded header
{ "success": true, "payer": "0xA11C...A11C", "transaction": "0x5e5e...7a1c", "network": "eip155:8453", "amount": "10000" }

steps.observable: Private: the response and its header stay between server and client; only the transaction hash points to public chain data.

steps.label: Publish the feedback file with proofOfPayment
steps.detail: The client writes the off-chain feedback file first: the required agentRegistry, agentId, clientAddress, createdAt, value and valueDecimals, plus optional tag1 and proofOfPayment {fromAddress, toAddress, chainId, txHash}. The proof lives only here, never on chain.
steps.controlPoint: After the fact: the client's own record of what it paid and why it scored the seller as it did.
steps.observable: Public once published: anyone with the feedbackURI can read the file, including the payer address and the transaction hash.

steps.label: giveFeedback(agentId, value, valueDecimals, tag1, tag2, endpoint, feedbackURI, feedbackHash)
steps.detail: The client computes feedbackHash (keccak256 of the file, optional for IPFS) and sends giveFeedback from its agentWallet if it is itself an agent. The client pays this gas unless an application sponsors it. The registry stores value, valueDecimals, tag1, tag2 and isRevoked only.
steps.observable: Public: NewFeedback event with agentId, clientAddress, feedbackIndex, value, valueDecimals, tags, endpoint, feedbackURI and feedbackHash.

failures.condition: The caller owns or operates the agent

steps.label: Fetch the file, check hash and txHash
steps.detail: An indexer or a later buyer that wants payment-backed feedback fetches the file from feedbackURI, compares its hash, and looks up txHash on the named chain to confirm payer, payee and amount. The registry does none of this.
steps.controlPoint: After the fact: score only feedback whose proof resolves to a real transfer to the agent's agentWallet, from reviewers you trust.
steps.observable: Public: subgraphs and explorers index NewFeedback; the file and the transfer are both public, so they can be joined.

failures.condition: The txHash does not exist or pays someone else
failures.outcome: Nothing on chain flags it and getSummary still counts the value; only off-chain scoring can discount it.
